# Results — Study 696 (Double-Bottom)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **two
troughs at a similar level, separated by a rally, mark an exhausted downtrend; buy the confirmed
breakout above the middle peak (the "neckline")** — tested with an **objective, mechanical**
detector on daily OHLC. Chart figures are partly subjective, so we test the closest rules-based
definition (two swing lows within a tolerance of one level, a genuine intervening rally, then a
confirmed neckline break) and say so. For each confirmed breakout we measure the forward
**5 / 10 / 20 / 40-day** return in the trade's intended (long) direction, **net of each name's own
base rate**, with a 1-day entry lag — plus the classic **measured-move target** hit rate and a
**long timer** that holds to target-or-timeout. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **auto-adjusted** (split + dividend) OHLC — SPY + 29 long-listed US large-caps (public, no key); the **same 30-name basket** as siblings 415 (triple top/bottom) and 695 (inverse head-and-shoulders) |
| As-of | **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; run 2026-07-10) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-30 (**21.5** years; **5,406** daily bars) |
| Panel | **30** names · quantlab fingerprint **`312be65a0274`** · sha1 fingerprint **`cac3bd6bbfcc`** |
| Detector | swing window 5; two troughs within **4%** of each other's level; intervening rally ≥ **5%**; figure span 15–150 bars; breakout = first close through the neckline (buffer 0), searched within 30 bars; non-overlapping |
| Breakouts | **560** confirmed double-**bottoms** (SPY: 12) |
| Timing / costs | enter the close **1 day after** the breakout (no look-ahead); hold 5/10/20/40 days for the headline, or to target-or-timeout (126 trading days ≈ 6 months) for the long timer; **5 / 10 bps** one-way × 2 legs |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** The basket is 30 names *still trading* in 2026. A
> fixed surviving-names panel cannot include names that delisted after a failed pattern, which
> tilts post-breakout forward returns mildly **up** — i.e. *for* the bullish double-bottom read.
> The effect we report is, if anything, generous to the figure.

## The headline — double-bottom (bullish, long) forward edge, EXCESS over base rate

The excess pools every confirmed breakout across the basket, subtracting each name's own
unconditional mean forward return (the base rate) so the test is "does the figure beat
buy-and-hold *for that name*", not "is the market up". *t* is one-sample; HAC *t* is Newey-West;
the placebo *p* is the share of **5,000 random-date entries** per name on the same tape whose
pooled excess **beats** the observed one.

| horizon | n | excess | raw | win-rate | one-sample *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | net (5 bps) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 558 | −0.073% | +0.218% | 52.0% | −0.48 | −0.49 | 0.541 | −0.173% |
| 10-day | 558 | **−0.379%** | +0.200% | 48.2% | **−1.91** | −1.98 | 0.643 | −0.479% |
| 20-day | 554 | +0.019% | +1.177% | 51.6% | +0.06 | +0.06 | 0.499 | −0.081% |
| 40-day | 550 | −0.478% | +1.814% | 51.1% | −1.12 | −1.18 | 0.594 | −0.578% |

Read it carefully. The excess is **never positive with a *t* ≥ 2** at any horizon — the closest
approach to significance is 10 days, and it is **negative** (*t* = −1.91): buying the confirmed
breakout *underperforms* the same stock's ordinary drift. The raw column is positive throughout
only because the names drift up on their own; once that drift is netted out there is nothing left
for the pattern to claim, and if anything the breakout slightly lags. The placebo agrees at every
horizon (*p* between 0.50 and 0.64 — a random date beats the pattern roughly half to two-thirds of
the time).

## Robustness — the (non-)edge is a tolerance artefact

If the figure were real, demanding a *cleaner* shape (tighter level tolerance, bigger intervening
rally) should *sharpen* it. It wanders around zero instead, and the *t* only ever brushes past 2
on the **wrong side**:

| tolerance | min bounce | n | excess (20-day) | *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 3% | 7% | 196 | +0.846% | +1.22 | 0.374 |
| **4%** | **5%** | **554** | **+0.019%** | **+0.06** | **0.501** |
| 6% | 3% | 1,304 | −0.357% | **−2.01** | 0.647 |

The strictest setting shows a positive-but-uncertified +0.85% (*t* = 1.22); the loosest setting is
mildly *negative* at *t* = −2.01. There is no strictness at which "two failures at one level"
becomes a reliable long signal.

## SPY-only — does the figure beat SPY buy-and-hold? (the README hook)

| horizon | n | excess | raw | *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 12 | +0.151% | +0.385% | +0.30 | 0.427 |
| 10-day | 12 | +0.219% | +0.686% | +0.30 | 0.417 |
| 20-day | 12 | +0.559% | +1.495% | +0.46 | 0.354 |
| 40-day | 12 | +1.843% | +3.710% | +1.02 | 0.140 |

On the index itself the detector fires only **12** times in 21.5 years — far too few to say
anything on its own, but every *t* stays well under 2. "Buy the SPY double-bottom breakout" is a
noisy non-event, consistent with the pooled basket result.

## The measured-move target — does the pattern's own height forecast a real move?

The classic charting recipe: project the trough-to-neckline height *up* from the neckline, and
that becomes the price target. For each of the 560 confirmed breakouts we check whether the
`high` touches that target within **126 trading days** (~6 months). The honest control is a
**magnitude-matched placebo**: random entries on the same tapes given a target of the *same*
relative size (drawn from the observed target-distance distribution) — a target that size should
already get hit some of the time on a pattern-blind random walk.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed hit rate | **452/560 = 80.7%** (Wilson 95% [77.2%, 83.8%]) |
| magnitude-matched placebo hit rate | **4,782/6,000 = 79.7%** |
| two-proportion *z* (observed vs placebo) | **+0.57** |
| median days to hit (when hit) | 21 |
| mean target distance from entry | +5.9% |

The 80.7% hit rate *looks* like a strong signal in isolation — but the honest control shows a
random walk asked to travel the **same typical distance** (+5.9%) over the same window already
clears the target **79.7%** of the time. The gap is **+1.0 point at *z* = +0.57** — nowhere near
significant. The "impressive" hit rate is almost entirely a function of the target being a modest,
achievable distance on a basket that drifts up over 21.5 years, not of the double-bottom shape
predicting anything.

## The long timer — hold to target-or-timeout, net of costs

Enter one day after the breakout; exit at the close of the day the `high` first touches the
target, else exit at the 126-day timeout close. One round trip = 2 × one-way cost × NAV, long
only, no borrow. The **excess** row races the trade against a **holding-period-matched base
rate** (buying the same name, unconditionally, for the same number of days) — the fair bar, for
exactly the reason spelled out on the headline table above.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| trades | 545 |
| gross per trade | **+2.942%** |
| net per trade (5 / 10 bps one-way) | **+2.842% / +2.742%** |
| one-sample *t* (vs 0) | **+7.80** |
| HAC *t* (vs 0) | **+8.87** |
| average holding period | 49.8 trading days |
| target-hit share (vs timeout) | 80.2% |
| **excess over a holding-period-matched base rate** | **+0.125%** |
| **HAC *t* of the excess (the decisive number)** | **+0.32** |

This is the desk's "direction trap," shown live. The **vs-zero** *t* of **+7.80** (HAC **+8.87**)
looks like a slam-dunk — but a 50-day-average hold on a basket that drifts up over two decades
*always* looks like that, pattern or no pattern. The fair comparison — the same names held
unconditionally for the same number of days — shows an excess of **+0.125% at HAC *t* = 0.32**:
statistically nothing. The long timer's gross P&L is the market's own beta wearing a pattern's
name, exactly as the measured-move hit-rate section already showed.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

On a deterministic panel with *planted* double bottoms, the same-tape placebo behaves exactly as
it must. Note the naive *t* is **positive but modest** at edge 0 — the figure's geometry
mechanically leaves the breakout price just above the neckline, so a raw *t* alone can be
misleading; **the placebo, not the raw *t*, is the arbiter**.

| world | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+1.57** (sd 0.76) | **p < 0.05 in 0/20 seeds** |
| null (edge = 0, single seed 696) | +2.12 | 0.344 |
| planted edge = +0.20 (large planted drift, seed 696) | **+10.32** | **0.009** |

With **no** planted drift the placebo is never beaten at the 5% level across 20 independent
seeds — even though a single-seed naive *t* can read as high as +2.12, which is exactly why the
placebo (not the raw *t*) decides the verdict. A large planted drift lights up hard (*t* = +10.32,
*p* = 0.009, win rate 72.3%). The harness can clearly bank a real edge — so the real tape's
uniformly-inside-noise result is a genuine **nothing**, not a power failure.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The double-bottom breakout excess never clears **t ≥ 2** in the pattern's
  favor at any horizon (−0.48 / **−1.91** / +0.06 / −1.12 for 5/10/20/40 days) and the closest
  approach to significance (10-day, *t* = −1.91) has the **wrong sign** — the breakout
  underperforms the stock's own drift. The random-date placebo is never beaten (*p* from 0.50 to
  0.64). The measured-move hit rate (80.7%) looks striking alone but is statistically
  indistinguishable from a magnitude-matched random walk (79.7%, *z* = 0.57). Robustness sweep
  finds no tolerance at which the edge turns reliably positive. Indistinguishable from noise once
  the tape's up-drift is netted out — and survivorship tilts *for* the figure, so this is
  generous.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The long-timer gross P&L (+2.94%/trade, *t* = 7.80 vs zero) looks
  compelling until raced against a holding-period-matched base rate: the excess collapses to
  **+0.125% at HAC *t* = 0.32**. There is no deployable edge, and costs (5–10 bps) only make the
  already-flat headline horizons worse.
- **"Target hit rate beats a coin flip of the same size?" — BUSTED.** The classic measured-move
  target is touched 80.7% of the time within six months — but a magnitude-matched placebo already
  gets there 79.7% of the time. The target's "accuracy" is a function of the target being a modest
  distance on a rising basket, not of the pattern's own predictive content.
